concepts.label: cbtransfer
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept for cbtransfer itself, though its two dependents (tool:cbbackup, tool:cbrestore) and its deprecation successor (tool:cbdatarecovery) were already extraction-layer. Deprecated generic ETL tool for transferring data between Couchbase clusters, backup directories, CSV files and Couchstore files.

notable_absence.finding: cbtransfer requires -u/-p but only warns generically that 'If you do not have a user account with permission to execute the command then it will fail with an unauthorized error' - no role or privilege is named, unlike cbrecovery.md (this batch's other cbtools/ page) which explicitly lists 'Full Administrator, Cluster Administrator, or XDCR Administrator'. The two pages' -u/-p option descriptions are otherwise near-identical in structure, which suggests cbrecovery's specific role list is the exception (XDCR credentials genuinely differ per cluster) rather than cbtransfer/cbworkloadgen's vague boilerplate being the exception - a templated sentence that was apparently never filled in with real role names on two of the three cbtools/ pages in this batch.

cross_component_finding: This page is the first in the corpus to state explicitly that cbbackup and cbrestore - both already extraction-layer tool: concepts, with cbbackup's own record already carrying the note 'legacy, superseded backup tool' - are literally built on top of cbtransfer, not siblings of it. It also connects cbtransfer forward to its own deprecation successor, tool:cbdatarecovery (already extraction-layer from a page in the sibling tools/ directory, not cli/cbtools/). Together this resolves what those two records left open: cbbackup, cbrestore, cbtransfer and cbdatarecovery form one architectural lineage - cbtransfer as the shared ETL engine underneath the first two, all three now deprecated in favor of cbdatarecovery - rather than four independent, disconnected tools.
cross_product_finding: No Capella-specific content; cbtransfer is explicitly deprecated and tied to local filesystem install paths and Couchstore file formats, none of which have a Capella surface.
